comments.body:
POINTER FOR A LATER READER — the click override this ticket's commit carried has its full analysis on
another ticket. Adding this only so the trail is followable; nothing here needs action, and the code on
main is correct and complete.

Commit 31844d5f9fb ("fix PYSEC-2026-2132 via click override") landed under this ticket, whose stated
purpose is the dependabot PRs. The inline comment it added to pyproject.toml is good and does carry the
REMOVE-WHEN condition ("Drop this override once inspect-ai lifts its cap upstream") plus the staleness
reason (inspect-ai caps click < 8.2.2 solely for pallets/click#3084, fixed upstream in click 8.3.2).

WHAT IS NOT ON MAIN, AND IS THE EXPENSIVE PART TO REDISCOVER, is on ticket e47e-a33d-b9cf-4421 (now
closed as a duplicate of this ticket, with six evidence comments retained):

 * **override-dependencies vs constraint-dependencies.** An attempt to verify the upgrade with
   `constraint-dependencies = ["click>=8.3.3"]` returns UNSATISFIABLE — and that result is MEANINGLESS,
   because constraint-dependencies can only NARROW an existing constraint set; it cannot lift a cap a
   dependency declares. `override-dependencies` REPLACES the requirement, which is why it works. A
   reader who repeats the constraint experiment will wrongly conclude the upgrade is impossible and may
   reach for a pip-audit `--ignore-vuln` suppression instead. That nearly happened here.
 * `uv lock --upgrade-package click` is a NO-OP for the same reason — it only permits movement inside
   the existing constraint set, so 8.2.1 really is the newest click satisfying inspect-ai. The resolver
   was never wrong and the uv version is irrelevant.
 * VERIFICATION THAT SHOULD BE REPEATED WHEN THE OVERRIDE IS REMOVED: `uv lock --check` under BOTH uv
   0.7.18 and 0.12.1 (the lock must stay at revision 2 — relocking with 0.12.1 rewrites it to revision 3
   with sweeping marker churn), `uv sync --locked --extra dev`, and `pip-audit --desc` over the whole
   resulting environment to confirm the old pin was masking nothing else.
 * SCOPE FACT worth knowing: override-dependencies is a workspace resolution directive and is NOT
   published in wheel metadata, so consumers installing nava-rebar[eval] from PyPI still get inspect-ai's
   own cap. The override moves only this repo's lock.

Also linked from e47e: 9fb3-ab66-2a81-4940 (the [eval]/inspect-ai path has no CI coverage and, because
`[tool.uv] conflicts` declares eval and dev mutually conflicting, structurally cannot get any from the
normal suite).

# Land dependabot PRs #123 (actions bumps) and #124 (mcp 2.0 + ruff 0.16.1) through Gerrit

## Problem

GitHub is a read-only mirror: dependabot still opens PRs there (#123, #124), but they can
never merge — the updates have to be re-landed as Gerrit changes and the PRs closed by
hand. Two are open now:

* **PR #123 — github-actions group**: `actions/setup-python` 6 -> 7 (new pinned SHA
  `5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97`) across 13 workflow files, plus a re-pin of
  `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` v1.14.0 to SHA `dc37677b2e1c63e2034f94d8a5b11f265b73ba33`
  (upstream re-tag; version unchanged). The change also updates the two `echo` allowlist
  lines (the pinned-action identity allowlist) that mirror those SHAs.
* **PR #124 — uv-lock group**: `mcp` 1.29.0 -> **2.0.0 (major)** — pyproject constraint
  loosened `>=1.28.1,<2` -> `<3` in both the `mcp` extra and the dev group, new transitive
  `mcp-types` package in `uv.lock` — and `ruff` `0.15.22` -> `0.16.1` (pinned in the dev
  group; ruff is what `make lint` and the pre-commit hook run).

The mcp major is the risk: `rebar-mcp` imports v1 API paths — `mcp.server.fastmcp.FastMCP`
(mcp_server.py:570, scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py:72), `mcp.server.auth.settings` /
`mcp.server.auth.provider` (mcp_server.py:590, _mcp_auth.py:38),
`mcp.server.transport_security` (mcp_server.py:512), `mcp.types.ToolAnnotations`
(_mcp_models.py:287). Whether 2.0 keeps these paths as compat shims is exactly what the
test suite must decide; the upstream migration guide lists every breaking change.

**P0 escalation (2026-08-02):** CI's gating `pip-audit` scan (\`_build-and-test.yml\`
`pip-audit` job — part of every `Verified` run) now fails on **click 8.2.1 →
PYSEC-2026-2132** (command injection in `click.edit()`; fix 8.3.3), which neither
dependabot PR covers (click is a transitive-only dependency — not constrained in
pyproject.toml, pinned only in `uv.lock`). Because the scan gates every Verified run,
EVERY change is blocked until the fixed lock lands — so this ticket gains a Change 0
that must land FIRST. Change 0's own Verified run scans Change 0's own committed lock,
so it can pass while everything else cannot; there is no circular block.

## What — three independently reviewable Gerrit changes

### Change 0 (P0, lands first) — click 8.3.3 lock bump

In the worktree: `uv lock --upgrade-package click` (expect click 8.2.1 -> >=8.3.3 in
`uv.lock` only; pyproject.toml is untouched since click is transitive), `uv sync
--all-extras`, then `pip-audit --desc` locally (must report no known vulnerabilities)
and the targeted suite for the CLI surface that consumes click plus `make lint` /
`make typecheck`. Push, wait for both votes (its Verified run proves the unblock),
Submit.

All changes carry this ticket's trailer and land through the normal gate
(`LLM-Review +1` + `Verified +1`, then Submit). Apply each PR's diff verbatim (`gh pr
diff N | git apply`), never retyped by hand, so the landed content is byte-identical to
what dependabot proposed (SHA pins included).

### Change A — PR #123 (workflows)

Apply `/tmp`-fetched `gh pr diff 123` onto a fresh worktree at current main. 13 workflow
files + the allowlist echo lines. No source code is touched; the `Verified` CI run on the
Gerrit change itself exercises the bumped `setup-python@v7` on every job that uses it —
that run IS the functional validation. Risk note: setup-python v7 migrated to ESM and
requires a node24 runner (ubuntu-latest provides it); no inputs we use were removed
(we do not pass `pip-install`).

### Change B — PR #124 (mcp 2.0 + ruff 0.16.1)

The `mcp>=1.28.1,<2` constraint has two consumers OUTSIDE pyproject.toml that PR #124's
diff does not touch and this change must keep coherent:

* `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml:105` installs `'mcp>=1.28.1,<2'` into a clean venv
  for the MCP-optionality job — on path 1 bump it to `,<3` in the same change (else CI
  exercises v1 while the package ships v2); on path 2 it stays `<2`, matching the kept
  pin.
* `docs/adr/0050-mcp-optional-auth-resource-server.md:28` records the `<2` pin and its
  rationale (DNS-rebinding fix GHSA-9h52-p55h-vw2f) — on path 1 amend the ADR text with
  a dated note that the ceiling moved to `<3` (the floor still covers the GHSA); on
  path 2 it stays accurate as written.

Apply `gh pr diff 124` (pyproject.toml + uv.lock) onto a fresh worktree, `uv sync
--all-extras`, then decide on evidence:

1. **Compat shims hold** (expected path): the full test suite (`make test` — the MCP
   surface that imports the at-risk v1 paths is covered by
   `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp*.py` — nine modules incl. `test_mcp.py`,
   `test_mcp_http_transport.py`, and the five `test_mcp_auth*` modules — plus
   `tests/interfaces/facades/test_workflow_mcp_schema.py`), `make
   lint` (now ruff 0.16.1), and `make typecheck` all pass — possibly after mechanical
   fixes (new ruff rules, import-path renames with 1:1 replacements, updated
   deprecation-warning filters). Mechanical fixes ride in the same change.
2. **Breakage is structural** (FastMCP/auth API gone or semantics changed): do NOT force
   the major through this ticket. Land the safe subset instead — ruff 0.16.1 bump +
   `uv.lock` refresh with mcp kept `<2` — comment the evidence (failing test names,
   import errors) on this ticket, and file a follow-up ticket for the mcp v2 migration
   linked `discovered_from` this one; PR #124 is then closed with a comment pointing at
   the landed subset + follow-up.

`ruff format --check` may newly fail on files 0.16.x formats differently; run
`.venv/bin/ruff format src/ tests/ scripts/` and include the mechanical reformat in the
change if so (it is what every subsequent commit's pre-commit hook will enforce).

### Closing the PRs

After each Gerrit change merges: `gh pr close <N> --comment "<landed as Gerrit change
<url>; GitHub is a read-only mirror>"`. Dependabot sees the manifest change on the next
mirror sync and stops re-opening.

## Scope

* IN: the two PR diffs, mechanical fixes needed to keep the gates green under the bumped
  ruff/mcp, closing PRs #123/#124 with provenance comments.
* OUT: any non-mechanical mcp v2 migration work (follow-up ticket if path 2 triggers);
  dependabot config changes; other open dependency updates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC0 (P0): a Gerrit change bumping click to >=8.3.3 in uv.lock is merged FIRST; its CI run's pip-audit step passes (PYSEC-2026-2132 cleared), unblocking all other changes.
- [ ] AC1: A Gerrit change with PR #123's diff (13 workflows + allowlist echo lines,
  byte-identical to `gh pr diff 123`) is merged with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`;
  the Verified run executed `actions/setup-python@v7` successfully.
- [ ] AC2: A Gerrit change for PR #124 is merged: either (path 1) the full diff with mcp
  2.0.0 + ruff 0.16.1 PLUS the two out-of-pyproject constraint consumers updated
  (`_optionality.yml:105` -> `,<3`; ADR 0050 amended with the ceiling-move note) and all
  of `make test`, `make lint`, `make typecheck` green, or (path 2) the documented safe
  subset (ruff bump, mcp kept `<2`, `_optionality.yml` and ADR 0050 untouched) plus a
  `discovered_from`-linked follow-up ticket for the mcp v2 migration.
- [ ] AC3: Both PRs #123 and #124 are closed on GitHub with a comment naming the Gerrit
  change(s) that landed the content.
- [ ] AC4: The decision evidence for Change B (test results under mcp 2.0) is recorded as a
  comment on this ticket.

## Verification commands

* `git diff <base>..HEAD -- .github/workflows | diff - /tmp/pr123.diff` (byte-fidelity, Change A)
* `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make test && make lint && make typecheck` (Change B, in its worktree)
* `gh pr view 123 --json state`, `gh pr view 124 --json state` -> `CLOSED`

PR 124: mcp 2.0.0 + new mcp-types transitive + ruff 0.16.1 lock refresh
